rules.sentence: Patients with unexplained shortness of breath or symptoms concerning for pulmonary hypertension should be thoroughly assessed.

The evaluation process should include a comprehensive medical and family history, physical examination, monitoring of blood pressure, heart rate, oxygen saturation, and blood tests, including brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) or N-terminal pro-BNP (NT-proBNP) and resting electrocardiogram (ECG).
The next step in the workup involves cardiac assessment with echocardiography.

Signs indicative of pulmonary dysfunction warrant pulmonary function tests (PFTs), chest imaging modalities like x-ray and computed tomography (CT), and, in some instances, cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET).
